section8_UNVERIFIED_CLAIMS.preamble: Every statement here is believed but NOT measured by this seat this session. This is the section most likely to cost the successor time if skipped.

claims.claim: McLennan's 48309:103671 BP-CONFORMANT-01 failure is the same class as Caldwell's 48055:1 (a roll-dropout on the old schema).
claims.basis: PURE INFERENCE from the shared rule id. NEVER DIAGNOSED. McLennan has only ONE CAD vintage (2025), so it CANNOT have a roll-dropout population -- which means this inference is probably WRONG and this parcel needs its own diagnosis.

claims.claim: Williamson will pass once the image is rebuilt.
claims.basis: NOTHING. Williamson has not been run against the corrected walk at all this session. It is gate-ready and that is all that is known.

claims.claim: CTX-ELGIN's residue probe (9 Bastrop / 457 Travis) and CTX-STAGE2's staged join (48 / 525) differ because the two registries are independently vintaged.
claims.basis: CTX-STAGE2's hypothesis, not verified. This seat found ONE concrete difference -- the hauska-engine registry's elgin-tx entry has NO layerWhere filter while the LDT registry has layerWhere CITY_LIMIT='ELGIN' -- but that difference would make the engine's staged set LARGER and therefore the residue SMALLER, which is the opposite of the observed direction. So the found difference does NOT explain the gap. Unresolved.

claims.claim: The three residue numbers (9/457, 48/525, and the rail's own) are measuring the same quantity.
claims.basis: PROBABLY FALSE and this may be most of the disagreement. CTX-ELGIN point-in-polygoned centroids against the LIVE ArcGIS service; CTX-STAGE2 joined against the STAGED table; the rail counts UNACCOUNTED CELLS, which excludes parcels already carrying an earned state from a prior sweep. Nobody has reconciled the three definitions.

orderingThatMatters: The image rebuild MUST come before any further county run. Every current walk failure is being graded by an image that predates PR #117. Re-running counties before rebuilding will reproduce the same failures and waste ~10 minutes each.

PE (property-explorer) had to be deployed BEFORE any production bake, because the declared-absence object crashes the InspectCard render. That deploy is DONE and verified, so this constraint is satisfied -- but if PE is ever rolled back, it re-arms.
ruledOutHypotheses: A read-after-write race between the bake and the serve was investigated and RULED OUT for McLennan: two consecutive walks produced byte-identical tallies, and the response headers showed X-Vercel-Cache: MISS, Age: 0, Cache-Control: max-age=0 must-revalidate. Do not re-open this line; the cause was the uncommitted classifier fix.
A Vercel edge cache holding stale payloads: ruled out by the same header read.
Bastrop having a missing-atom population: ruled out by direct measurement (77,799 of 77,799 conformant).
trapsLearned: gcloud is a .cmd on this machine; node's execFileSync cannot spawn it (EINVAL). Pass secrets through the environment from bash instead.
Multi-line string matching against these source files fails silently because the working copies are CRLF. Patch by LINE INDEX, not by multi-line string replace. This cost several cycles.
Backticks inside bash heredocs get command-substituted and corrupt inserted code. Write patch scripts to a file and run them.
Two heredocs in one bash command (e.g. `cat <<A ... && git commit -F - <<B`) break the parser. Split them.
A long-running query at near-zero CPU is STUCK, not working. CTX-STAGE2 lost over an hour to this; process inspection is the tell.
The Factory store times out on six-county aggregate queries while a bake is running. Query one county at a time with an explicit statement_timeout.
judgementsNotWrittenDown: The jurisdiction cohort samples prop_id ASCENDING, which biases toward low-numbered and therefore old/degenerate parcels. This is WHY 48055:1 keeps surfacing. It was deliberately NOT changed -- adjusting a sampler to avoid a failure it correctly found is sampling around the problem. A successor may be tempted to 'fix' this; it is not a bug.

The DECLARED_LAYER_GAP ceiling of 9/457 was written from CTX-ELGIN's numbers WITHOUT checking they described the same population the rail measures. That is the actual root of the Bastrop/Travis block. The ceiling is not wrong to refuse -- the ceiling was wrong to be written.

Every one of this seat's five significant errors this session reduces to one habit: trusting a characterisation (a code comment, a lane's close, a function's apparent return shape) instead of reading the thing itself. A successor inheriting this program should assume any number quoted from a close is a claim about a different population until re-measured.
